newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pares losses by close, industry seen.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pares losses by close, industry seen.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures pared losses in the afternoon on light roaster buying on the dips but the market still ended Friday lower.
Sentiment was also helped by a rebound on the New York arabica futures from 10-week lows on Thursday on spec long liquidation.
But overall activity in London remained dull, with players seen rolling out their July positions ahead of the first notice day on Tuesday.
The July/Sept spread widened to $15 at the close from $6 at Thursday's close.
September finished the day $16 down at $1,785 a tonne after a low at $1,750.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday a warm, subtropical ridge of high pressure continued to dominate Brazil's coffee belt blocking any cold weather from entering the region.
Low temperatures ranged from 54-64 F (12-18 C).
"The main danger is now that it is so warm that the predicted rains could actually lead to flowerings three months ahead of normal," broker GNI said.
With Brazil escaping damaging frost so far and funds moving out of coffee futures, traders said the market looked set to test lower levels.
One said: "It looks like a one-way street for coffee now. It's very difficult to be bullish."
In other news, the influential Colombian Coffee Federation celebrates its 70th annivesary on Friday.
